LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can we extract information from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary from a text for information
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify vocabulary from a text for information
   In simple words: practise until you can identify vocabulary from a text for information. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension
   In simple words: practise until you can respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues.
4. Show that you can: identify vocabulary from a text for information

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to an audio recording of a dialogue related to the theme,
2. Read the summarised key information in class for peer review,
3. Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner listens to an audio recording of a dialogue related to the theme.
4. Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner is motivated to learn continually by building a vocabulary bank based on the words identified. 52 Values:
5. Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to paraphrase the key ideas from the text.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify vocabulary from a text for information
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
